newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND MULLS TAX WRITE-OFFS FOR BOND BUYERS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND MULLS TAX WRITE-OFFS FOR BOND BUYERS.

text.p: The Polish government will consider whether to reintroduce relief on personal income tax for buyers of Treasury bonds because sales are not going well, a Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.

"Our goal is to finance the budget in the best way. If bond sales prove very small this year, something will have to be done...Tax write-offs are one solution," the ministry's public debt department director, Piotr Dziewulski, told Reuters.
He added that in his personal view the tax relief should apply to individuals buying bonds with maturities longer than three years.
But he said it might prove difficult to reintroduce the measure by next year because of the parliamentary elections scheduled on September 21.
"October is the latest date for proposing changes to the tax law and (during that period) we are likely to see talks on formation of a new government," Dziewulski said.
From this year Poland abandoned a regulation allowing people to deduct investment in government bonds, up to a certain level, from income tax in order to simplify the tax system.
But as a result sales of bonds, notably those with a one-year maturity, dropped.
